Triage: type Bug, `domain:ui`, **`pm:blocked`**.

Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#10749

Rationale: the card's own recommendation (B — trim at the producer) is also the platform convention: the visibility declaration is authoritative where it is written, and a client-side trim is consumer-side compensation that cannot fix the wire. The server half already has a home — objectstack#10749 (`payload_json` carries `hidden` fields to the approver) — so this card should not be dispatched as option A. On unlock (when #10749 lands): re-verify the summary card against a snapshot produced by the fixed producer; if the wire no longer carries hidden fields, this closes with a verification note and no objectui code change; only if a client-side reason survives does A come back — and that return trip is a re-triage, not a default.

Unlock scan (triage seat, session `session_01Nd9biL1MqkZT5tzgTEp7AB`, 2026-08-24 hourly round): upstream `Blocked-by:` objectstack#10749 closed today — `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`. That line is exhausted.

**The upstream ruling re-prices this card's A/B fork — re-read objectstack#10749's closing comment before dispatch:**
- Maintainer ruling, verbatim: "**`hidden: true` stays UI-only; `internal: true` is the serialization primitive**". `hidden` gains no serialization semantic.
- ⇒ **Direction B (server-side trim of `hidden` when writing/serving `payload_json`) is foreclosed** — that would be exactly the serialization semantic the ruling refused. Fields an author wants out of read results are declared `internal: true`, which never reaches the wire at all.
- ⇒ **Direction A is the ruled shape, and it is not a workaround**: `hidden` is a *UI contract* ("Hidden from default UI"), and this drawer summary card is default UI — honouring the declaration client-side is the UI enforcing its own contract, the only place that contract lives.
- Post-landing surface change: FLS-restricted fields no longer arrive in the served payload (serve-time redaction via `getReadableFields`, objectstack PR #11039 — both doors). What still arrives and still renders is the non-FLS `hidden: true` field — this card's remaining subject.

**Scope reminder from the card, still true:** the prerequisite is a metadata read reaching this page (`useObjectFields` is unexported app-shell internals), so this is a wiring + filter change, not a filter tweak. Re-verify the render path on the post-#11039 ref before dispatch.

Type Bug, `domain:ui`, dispatchable.

If you find a route that needs no new export, say that too; it is the cheaper answer.

Disjoint by full path.

## ⛔ RULED UPSTREAM — the A/B fork is re-priced, and B is FORECLOSED

This card sat `pm:blocked` behind objectstack#10749, which **closed today**. Its closing ruling changes the answer, so ⛔ **do not implement the card body's own recommendation** — the card recommends **B**, and B is now ruled out.

**Maintainer ruling, verbatim: 「`hidden: true` stays UI-only; `internal: true` is the serialization primitive」.**

What follows, carried from the triage unlock scan:

- ⛔ **Direction B (server-side trim of `hidden` when writing or serving `payload_json`) is foreclosed** — that is exactly the serialization semantic the ruling refused. `hidden` gains **no** serialization semantic. Fields an author wants out of read results are declared **`internal: true`**, which never reaches the wire at all.
- ✅ **Direction A is the ruled shape, and it is NOT a workaround.** `hidden` is a **UI contract** ("Hidden from default UI"), and this drawer summary card **is** default UI. Honouring the declaration client-side is the UI enforcing its own contract — the only place that contract lives.
- ⚠️ This inverts the card's AGENTS.md #0.1 argument, and you should understand why rather than just obeying: a client-side trim is consumer-side compensation **only when the producer shipped data it should not have**. Under this ruling the producer is correct to ship it — `hidden` was never a wire concern — so the UI is the *authoritative* enforcement point, not a compensating one.

## What the upstream landing already changed — re-measure, do not assume

- **FLS-restricted fields no longer arrive in the served payload** (serve-time redaction via `getReadableFields`, objectstack PR #11039 — both doors). ⛔ Those are no longer your subject.
- **What still arrives and still renders is the non-FLS `hidden: true` field.** That is this card's remaining subject, and it may be a smaller set than the card describes. ⚠️ **Re-verify the render path on the post-#11039 ref before writing code.** If the defect no longer reproduces at all, ⛔ **stop and report** — this card would then close with a verification note and no objectui code change, which the original triage explicitly named as a legitimate outcome.

## The measured starting point (card's own reading — re-derive it)

`payloadSummary` in `apps/console/src/pages/system/ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx` builds the summary card from the request's `payload_json` snapshot, filtering: `PAYLOAD_SYSTEM_KEYS` (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `organization_id`); the lead amount key; `null`/object/empty values; unresolved opaque ids (15+ chars with no `payload_display` entry); then **the first 6 survivors**. **There is no field-visibility filter in that list.**

⚠️ **The 6-field cut is a confounder in both directions.** A `hidden` field only renders if it survives to the first 6, so a fixture that happens to place it seventh proves nothing, and a "fixed" summary that merely reordered fields is not a fix. Pin on the filter, not on what the card happens to render.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not assume

1. **The prerequisite is a wiring change, not a filter tweak** — the card measured that `ApprovalsInboxPage` holds no field-level metadata at all (every `hidden` occurrence in the file is a Tailwind class, an `aria-hidden`, or prose). Re-derive that; if a metadata read has since been wired into this page by other work, the fix is much smaller and you should say so.
2. **Cost is part of the ruled shape.** Direction A "costs a metadata read per drawer open (or a cached one)". Measure which you are shipping and state it. ⛔ A per-open uncached read on a drawer an approver opens repeatedly is a real cost — if you cache, say what invalidates it.
3. ⚠️ **`hidden` and `internal` are now distinct primitives with distinct meanings.** ⛔ Do not filter on `internal` here, and ⛔ do not conflate them in prose or in code. If the object metadata reaching this page carries both, filter on **`hidden`** and leave `internal` to the wire, per the ruling.
4. **Related card #5553** (the "Raw data (JSON)" panel gate) is **separate and unaffected either way** — ⛔ do not touch that surface or reopen its ruling.

## Verification

The pin must be the **filter**, not the render. Predict the direction **before** running: a fixture whose snapshot carries a field the object declares `hidden: true` must not reach the summary card — red before your fix, green after. **Counter-probe required, and it is the important half:** a non-hidden field in the same fixture, in the same position, **must still render**. Without it, "the hidden field is gone" is satisfiable by breaking the summary card entirely, and the positive assertion cannot tell the difference.

Reverse-verify: revert the filter and show the assertion goes red. Prove the mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and separately** the removed text (an editor's exit code proves nothing on a zero-hit anchor). Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`; confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` is empty afterwards.

⚠️ **Run app-shell path-filtered.** Whole-package vitest there is ~784 s and holds the shared lock — ⛔ do not run it. Use `pnpm exec vitest run <paths>` from the repo root (this repo's vitest guard refuses the `--filter` forms). Gates by name with exit codes: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` (⚠️ hyphenated `type-check`; echo the script name so a zero-match silent pass cannot read as green — and note that a first RED reading `Cannot find module @object-ui/...` is the **unbuilt-closure signature**, not a real failure: build the dependency closure and re-read), the path-filtered vitest, and eslint on changed files with the delta against merge-base stated.

Changeset required if any published package's surface moves (app-shell's barrel); run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing, and remember empty frontmatter is this repo's "releases nothing" declaration. Draft PR, `Fixes #5565`. ⛔ Do not mark it ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ do not enable auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — this repo's sanitizer eats them) and return it.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**

PR #6031, head `588c2c5a5`, merge-base `c0091b82b`. Gate read at the usual mark.

### Clause-② — answered better than the dispatch anticipated, and I verified it

I priced this card as *"likely yes"* on the assumption the fix would have to export `useObjectFields` from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`. **It did not, and there is no widening at all.** I checked directly: `git diff --name-only … -- 'packages/**'` returns **nothing**. Zero packages touched; all five files are in `apps/console` plus a changeset.

✅ And the route you found is better than the one the card sketched, for a reason worth recording: `useObjectFields` reads through the metadata-admin `MetadataClient`, whereas a page-local seam over `useAdapter` + `getObjectSchema` is **already exported, already consumed by this page's sibling `recordReadability.ts`, and is the runtime read every record form already performs for an ordinary business user.** So the fix rides an existing, already-authorised path instead of publishing an admin-flavoured hook to reach it. ⛔ The cheaper answer was available and you found it — that was the explicit invitation in the dispatch and it is the right outcome.

### The ruling, carried correctly

Direction **A** implemented, **B** untouched. The filter reads `hidden` only; `internal` is not read anywhere. ✅ The two primitives stayed distinct, which is exactly what the upstream ruling turns on.

✅ **PM assumption 1 re-derived rather than inherited:** `payloadSummary` still has no field-visibility filter, and the page still held no field-level metadata (every `hidden` occurrence before this change is a Tailwind class, an `aria-hidden`, or prose). Re-verified on the post-#11039 ref, as instructed.

✅ **The 6-field cut confounder was handled the right way round.** I warned that a "fixed" summary which merely reordered fields is not a fix. Dropping the hidden keys **before** the cut means the seventh field is **promoted into the freed slot** rather than the card shrinking — and the pin asserts the promotion, not merely the absence. That is the difference between "the hidden field is gone" and "the hidden field is gone and nothing else changed."

### The scope extension — **ratified**

You also trimmed `decisionAmountEntry` at the drawer call site. That is beyond the literal fence, and it is **correct**, on the argument you gave: it sits in the same "Business summary card" JSX block, reads the same snapshot, and trimming only the field grid would have **relocated a hidden amount-like field into the bold figure at the top of the very card being repaired**. A fix that moves a leak from the grid to the headline is not a fix. Same defect class, same mechanical guard, same gate family, named in the PR body — that is the standard for a bounded in-place exemption in this lane, and it is met.

✅ Ablation A proves the coupling is real rather than asserted: removing the `payloadSummary` guard turned **two** tests red, the second being *"does not lead with an amount field the object declares hidden"* — because `decisionAmountEntry` still drops the amount, leaving `excludeKey` undefined so the ungated grid re-renders that same figure **by a different route**. Predicting that second failure *before* running, and for that reason, is the part that shows the two guards are one mechanism.

### The fail-open judgement — **A stands, and this is not me ruling a product question**

You flagged it rather than burying it, which was right. My disposition:

**A (shipped) follows from the maintainer's own ruling** rather than from a preference of mine. 「`hidden: true` stays UI-only; `internal: true` is the serialization primitive」 strips `hidden` of any wire or access semantic; FLS is the access control and objectstack PR #11039 already redacts at serve time, both doors. So an unanswered metadata read is a **presentation** unknown, not a **permission** unknown — and blanking an approver's decision surface on a transient metadata hiccup would be a real harm bought with no security benefit.

✅ Your contrast with #5553 is the load-bearing distinction and it is correct: **#5553 fails closed because its measured defect *was* a non-holder seeing the panel — a security stake.** Here there is no such stake left, by the ruling's own construction. ✅ And it matches the sibling probe on this very page (`recordReadability` fails open, explicitly reasoned), so the page does not now hold two conflicting postures.

✅ Pinning it by a test **named** `FAILS OPEN` is what makes it a decision rather than an accident — trivially invertible if the maintainer ever wants the #5553 posture, and impossible to flip by accident.

### #6020 is a sharper finding than the card it came from

> the approvals inbox **QUEUE rows** still render an amount field the object declares `hidden: true`, **and the `sortKey === 'amount'` comparator still orders on it** — leaking the relative magnitude of a hidden field even where the figure is not shown.

The **ordering** half is the part neither the card nor my dispatch saw. A hidden field that is not displayed but *is* sorted on still leaks its relative magnitude to anyone who can read the row order — a channel that survives every "don't render it" fix. ✅ Correctly not folded in, with a real cost argument (N rows × K objects is `recordReadability`'s batching cost model, not the single cached read added here) and a real acceptance argument (changing a sort is an ordering change with its own criteria). ✅ Dedupe search run first, `bug` + `domain:ui`, no `pm:queue` — filed for triage to schedule, not self-graded into the queue.

### Cost, stated as the ruling requires

One `getObjectSchema` per distinct object per mount, landing on the adapter's `MetadataCache` (LRU 100, 5-minute TTL, in-flight de-duplication), plus a per-mount read-once ledger so re-renders cost nothing; invalidated by that TTL, an adapter `clearCache()` (the shell issues one on locale switch), or a reload. ✅ "Measure which you ship and state it, and if you cache say what invalidates it" — answered in full.

### Two more credited

- ✅ **The first `console` type-check RED was correctly *not* dismissed as the unbuilt-closure trap.** It was `TS2322` on a fixture's literal-inferred row type — a genuine failure, distinguished from the `Cannot find module @object-ui/...` signature by reading the error rather than the exit code. The trap warning in the dispatch is there to prevent panic, not to license waving red away.
- ✅ **Every denial case additionally asserts four sibling business fields, so an empty card fails before it can pass** — that is the counter-probe requirement satisfied structurally rather than by one extra test, and it closes the "satisfiable by breaking the summary card entirely" hole exactly.
